description: Twelve arithmetic results worked out from two input voltages, all computed at once and all available together.

inputs.text: The voltage called A in every result; the number of channels patched here sets the module's polyphony.
The voltage called B in every result.

outputs.text: A and B added together and halved.
A divided by B, or 0V whenever B is at 0V.
B divided by A, or 0V whenever A is at 0V.
A raised to the power of B.
One divided by A, or 0V whenever A is at 0V.
One divided by B, or 0V whenever B is at 0V.

notes: Both A and B must be patched. With either one empty no output is written at all, so each jack holds whatever it last carried, which is 0V on a freshly placed module.
No output is limited, so multiplying two large voltages or raising one to a power can produce voltages far outside the ±10V a module normally sends.
